core_obligations: Record that one direction was already obtained, and use the statement for countable indexedness alone to reduce to the case where both spaces are countably indexed (proof lines 4602-4606).
Write both spaces as formal spectra of weakly admissible algebras, convert the morphism into a continuous algebra homomorphism, and note that it is taut (proof lines 4606-4612).

For an open ideal of the target, let I be the closure of its image in the source, identify the corresponding fibre product of spectra by two earlier lemmas, and observe that the resulting map of quotients is faithfully flat because the morphism is surjective and flat (proof lines 4614-4621).
Conclude by the descent statement for weakly admissible rings, whose hypotheses have now been met (proof lines 4623-4625).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the countably indexed case (proof lines 4602-4606).
Formal spectra and a taut ring map (proof lines 4606-4612).
The fibre product computation and faithful flatness of the quotients (proof lines 4614-4621).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces which is representable, surjective and flat, the lemma asserts that the source is countably indexed and classical if and only if the target is (statement lines 4596-4600). One direction was already obtained as part of an earlier statement of the chapter, and the proof concentrates on the converse. By the corresponding statement for countable indexedness alone one may assume both spaces are countably indexed, hence formal spectra of weakly admissible algebras, and the morphism corresponds to a continuous algebra homomorphism which representability and affineness make taut (proof lines 4602-4614). The reduction to the ring-theoretic situation is then completed by computing a fibre product: for an open ideal of the target with closure of its image in the source, the corresponding fibre product of spectra is identified using two earlier lemmas, and since the morphism is surjective and flat the resulting map between the quotients is faithfully flat, so the homomorphism has exactly the shape required by the section on taut descent (proof lines 4614-4623). The conclusion follows from the descent statement for weakly admissible rings (proof lines 4623-4625). The claim is H2: after the reduction of countable indexedness, the argument identifies a fibre product and checks faithful flatness, which is what makes the taut descent statement applicable; each step is named.
